text:
cam: Hi team — new hire here. On Win11 + WSL2, trying to boot the dev compose. Postgres container shows port mapping `0.0.0.0:5434->5432/tcp` but my local app (running on Windows host) can't connect to localhost:5434, get connection refused. Any quick debugging tips?

olivia: welcome! first check if something else is using 5434 (`netstat -ano | findstr 5434`). Also confirm docker ps shows the mapping.

cam: docker ps shows the mapping and `docker exec db pg_isready` returns ok. netstat shows nothing listening on 5434 on host.

ben: on WSL2 Docker Desktop sometimes publishes ports to the WSL VM interface rather than Windows loopback. Try `localhost` and `host.docker.internal` both. If your app runs in Windows (not WSL) try `localhost`; if it runs inside WSL use `host.docker.internal`.

cam: tried host.docker.internal:5434 — still fails. localhost works though! Weird.

infra-bot: infra-bot posted: "detected possible firewall rule blocking Docker NAT on cam-win11"

nora: Good to note: Windows Defender firewall sometimes blocks the Docker NAT. If a restart doesn't help, toggling the firewall or restarting Docker Desktop often fixes it. Also avoid mounting Postgres data on NTFS path; use a named volume or move repo into WSL filesystem to avoid permission errors.

cam: Restarted Docker Desktop and then localhost connected fine. I also replaced the bind mount with a named volume per the tips and fixed a `could not change permissions` error. I'll open a tiny PR to add a short checklist for Windows WSL dev: 1) prefer named volumes or keep repo inside WSL fs, 2) try localhost vs host.docker.internal depending on where the app runs, 3) restart Docker Desktop if published ports appear unreachable. Thanks for the help! :tada:
